prompt: Let $R\subseteq A\times A$, with all quantified variables ranging over $A$. Which property is defined exactly by $\forall x\forall y\forall z\; ((R(x,y)\land R(y,z))\Rightarrow R(x,z))$?

answers.explanation: Every two-step chain has its direct shortcut, including chains with repeated vertices.
Every element has a self-loop; pairs of different elements are unrestricted. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
Every related pair has its reverse; loops are allowed but not required. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
Mutual relatedness forces equality. Self-loops are allowed. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
Every two-step chain lacks its direct shortcut. Failure of transitivity instead requires at least one chain without its shortcut. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
Two outgoing neighbours of the same element must be related in the indicated direction. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
Every pair of distinct elements is comparable in at least one direction. This convention imposes no condition on loops. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
Some two-step chain lacks its shortcut; other chains may have shortcuts. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
An element has at most one outgoing related element; it need not have any. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
Each element has at least one outgoing related element, which may be itself. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
